pm_exper_user_2883_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Because pollen and dust trigger your seasonal allergic rhinitis, running during early dawn hours — before pollen counts peak — can minimize symptoms. You could also rinse your face and change clothes immediately afterward to remove allergens that cling to skin and fabric.
(b) With your pollen- and dust-induced allergic rhinitis, try sticking to paved park paths away from dense flower beds or freshly cut grass. Sunglasses and a cap can add a protective barrier, reducing how much pollen reaches your eyes and airways during the run.
(c) For more comfortable spring runs, try going early in the morning or after rainfall to avoid peak allergen periods. Wearing sunglasses and a cap can help shield against airborne particles, and a quick shower afterward will leave you feeling refreshed.
(d) Since your seasonal allergic rhinitis flares up with pollen and dust, consider checking the pollen forecast and scheduling your runs right after a light morning rain, when airborne particles are lower. Wearing a lightweight, breathable mask can also help filter allergens while you enjoy the park.
